decision: measured the color loss: ka writes 24-bit color codes unconditionally, 350 in its first frame, for four different terminal identities; no code reads what the terminal can show

decision: acceptance bar. Sizes: 46x14 and 40x12 are the phone with the keyboard up, 50x28 portrait without it, 88x20 landscape, plus the sizes the harness asserts today. Depths: 24-bit, 256, sixteen. Usable on a phone: with nothing open the transcript keeps at least three quarters of the rows; with a popup or modal open the input line and at least 5 list rows stay visible; no two bordered boxes touch; ka's own hints drop whole, never cut; prose gets at least nine tenths of the columns after its indent. At 56 columns and 18 rows or more, every existing frame stays byte-identical. Color: at 256 depth no 24-bit code leaves the process and text contrast stays within ten percent of 24-bit; at sixteen depths no accent becomes black, white or gray
why: a bar written before the build is what the frames are judged against

decision: prototyped the color fitting in Python against the real palette: at 256 colors nearest-color keeps 22 of 30 palette colors distinct and text contrast unchanged; at sixteen the selection and hover fills landed on pure red, so colors with an OKLab lightness under 0.40 become the terminal's black (every surface and plain border in the palette is under 0.35, the focus border is at 0.57)
why: choosing by evidence rather than by taste
evidence: prototype run in a shell heredoc, nothing on disk

decision: mocked three layouts at 46x14 as text grids and chose A, slim chrome: the transcript gets 11 of 14 rows (today 5 to 7); B with the header merged into the status line gets 12 and C with a header that hides gets 13
why: all three clear the bar of three quarters of the rows; A is the smallest structural change and keeps the touch-scroll arrows and the session line where a desktop user knows them
evidence: /tmp/ka-narrow/variants.png (temporary; the grids are in the log's history)

decision: the layout mode has two independent switches: short when the frame has fewer than 18 rows (no air rows, a bare composer line, a smaller todo panel), narrow when it has fewer than 56 columns (no side air, inset or scrollbar rail in the transcript, a shorter placeholder, overlays spanning the frame)
why: the two shortages are independent: a portrait phone without the keyboard is narrow with rows to spare, a laptop with a short window is short with columns to spare; below 18 rows the fixed chrome took more than 40 percent of the frame

decision: adjusted the color bar: text contrast at 256 colors must stay at 4.5 to 1 or better and within 15 percent of 24-bit, where the bar first said 10 percent
why: my own test measured the error text on the error panel at 5.38 before and 4.75 after, a loss of 12 percent, because the palette has no entry near that dark red tint; every other pair is within a few percent; the requirement underneath the number is that text stays readable
